title: Opposite of a fixed cocone category and colimit-limit duality
statement:
Use coherent diagrams, cone/cocone categories, initial/terminal objects and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], opposites and their mapping-space equivalences from clause (4) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence], and the internal-functor reversal of [lem-coef-infinity-cocone-opposite-join-functor]. Let $K$ be a small simplicial set, $\mathcal E$ a quasicategory in a containing universe, and $F:K\to\mathcal E$ a fixed diagram. Write $D=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)$, $D'=\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}})$, and $F^o=F^{\mathrm{op}}$. There is a natural simplicial isomorphism
$$\bigl(\{F\}\times_{D,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,D)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,D}\mathcal E\bigr)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}\times_{D',\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,D')\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,D'}\{F^o\},$$
where the maps from $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ are the constant-diagram maps. The isomorphism reverses the parameter simplex and the interval, exchanges endpoint evaluations, and commutes with apex evaluation. On vertices it sends $\lambda:F\to\Delta_Kx$ to $\lambda^o:\Delta_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}x\to F^o$. Under this isomorphism, $\lambda$ is colimiting (initial in its fixed-$F$ cocone category) if and only if $\lambda^o$ is limiting (terminal in its fixed-$F^o$ cone category). The induced mapping-space equivalences identify outgoing spaces from $\lambda$ with incoming spaces to $\lambda^o$, naturally in the other cocone; their contractibility is equivalent. The assertions include $K=\varnothing$ and require no other colimits or limits in $\mathcal E$.

source.place: Construction 1.4.2.2 (opposite simplicial set); Remark 7.1.6.2 in https://kerodon.net/tag/02KF for limit/colimit duality. The displayed fixed coherent comma-category isomorphism is agent-formulated from def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones, not attributed to the sharp relative-cone definition. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copies WANTED. Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: Write $C_F$ for the fixed-$F$ cocone pullback and $L_{F^o}$ for the fixed-$F^o$ cone pullback in the statement, using [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Clause (4) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence] makes $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ a quasicategory. Since both $K$ and $K^{\mathrm{op}}$ are small, [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] applies to $(K,\mathcal E)$ and $(K^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}})$: $D,D',C_F,L_{F^o}$ are quasicategories. No completeness or cocompleteness assumption occurs in these assertions.

source.place: Construction 1.4.2.2 and agent setup for coherent comma categories; the cited calculus supplies the quasicategory and Kan assertions.

proof.text:
Let $\rho_n:\Delta^n\xrightarrow{\cong}(\Delta^n)^{\mathrm{op}}$ denote the vertex-reversal isomorphism used in [lem-coef-infinity-cocone-opposite-join-functor]. By [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], an $n$-simplex of $C_F$ is a pair $a:\Delta^n\to\mathcal E$, $h:K\times\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal E$ with $h|_0=F\operatorname{pr}_K$ and $h|_1=a\operatorname{pr}_{\Delta^n}$. Opposite preserves products degree by degree, directly from its definition in clause (4) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence]. Set $a^o=a^{\mathrm{op}}\rho_n$ and
$$h^o=h^{\mathrm{op}}(\mathrm{id}_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}\times\rho_n\times\rho_1):K^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\longrightarrow\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}.$$
This is precisely the internal-functor reversal of the cited node, with the interval also reversed. Since $\rho_1$ exchanges $0,1$, $h^o|_0=a^o\operatorname{pr}_{\Delta^n}$ and $h^o|_1=F^o\operatorname{pr}_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}$. Thus $(a^o,h^o)$ is an $n$-simplex of $L_{F^o}$, not merely an equivalence class of such simplices. In degree zero it is exactly the asserted transformation $\lambda^o:\Delta_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}x\to F^o$.

source.place: Construction 1.4.2.2; explicit agent construction on the coherent comma pullbacks, using the internal-functor reversal already stated in the DAG.

proof.text:
For $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, put $\alpha^\vee(i)=n-\alpha(m-i)$ as in clause (4) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence]. Vertexwise,
$$\rho_n\Delta(\alpha)=(\Delta(\alpha^\vee))^{\mathrm{op}}\rho_m,$$
since both send $i$ to $n-\alpha(i)$. Substituting this equality in the formulas of step 2 shows that restricting a source simplex by the operator $\alpha^\vee$ and then reversing is the same as reversing and then restricting by $\alpha$. These are exactly the operators of $C_F^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $L_{F^o}$. Hence step 2 defines a simplicial map $\Phi:C_F^{\mathrm{op}}\to L_{F^o}$. Repeating the construction reverses each parameter, interval and shape twice, recovering $a,h$ in every degree, so it defines the inverse. The apex coordinate is $a\mapsto a^o$, proving commutation with apex evaluation. Restricting the displayed formula to either interval endpoint proves exchange of endpoint evaluations. Precomposition in $K$ and postcomposition in $\mathcal E$ commute with the formula, proving its naturality. All these are equalities of the prescribed simplex data.

source.place: Construction 1.4.2.2; elementary operator, involution, endpoint and naturality checks on the explicit formula.

proof.text:
For any two vertices $\lambda,\mu$ of $C_F$, clause (4) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence], applied to the quasicategory $C_F$, gives the natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{C_F}(\lambda,\mu)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{C_F^{\mathrm{op}}}(\mu,\lambda).$$
Applying $\Phi$ gives an isomorphism of the latter right-pinched mapping simplicial set with $\operatorname{Map}_{L_{F^o}}(\mu^o,\lambda^o)$: postcomposition by a simplicial isomorphism and its inverse preserves exactly the constant-face and last-vertex conditions in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. This construction is natural in $\mu$, because the opposite mapping-space equivalence is natural and the second map is induced by the single simplicial map $\Phi$. The two spaces are weakly contractible simultaneously: a weak equivalence induces bijections on components and isomorphisms on based homotopy groups, so either both or neither have one component and trivial homotopy groups. As $\Phi$ is bijective on vertices, $\mu^o$ ranges over every cone on $F^o$ when $\mu$ ranges over every cocone on $F$. The definition of initial object in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] therefore identifies initiality of $\lambda$ in $C_F$ with terminality of $\lambda^o$ in $L_{F^o}$. Its definitions of colimiting and limiting give the asserted equivalence.

source.place: Agent mapping-space proof from clause (4) of the cited opposite-equivalence node and the stated definitions; compare Remark 7.1.6.2 in https://kerodon.net/tag/02KF for sharp-cone limit/colimit duality, not for an identification of comma categories.

proof.text: If $K=\varnothing$, then $K^{\mathrm{op}}=\varnothing$ and $D=D'=\Delta^0$: in every degree there is exactly one map from the empty simplicial set. The pullbacks of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] thus give $C_F=\mathcal E$ and $L_{F^o}=\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ canonically, and the preceding construction is their evident opposite identification. The universal-property assertion becomes the initial/terminal correspondence just proved. For a general $K$ the proof constructs an isomorphism between the two categories whether or not either contains a universal object; it never chooses an unrelated limit or colimit.

source.place: Agent check of the empty-shape case directly from the coherent comma definitions; compare Example 7.1.6.5 in https://kerodon.net/tag/02KF.

proof_origin.place: Explicit opposite reversal of the coherent comma pullbacks, using the existing internal-functor reversal and opposite mapping-space equivalences; comparison with Remark 7.1.6.2 in https://kerodon.net/tag/02KF. The comma result is not attributed to the sharp-cone reference.
